scenario.name: Sophos X-Ops, Trend Micro & Group-IB — Qilin (Agenda) Ransomware: GPO PowerShell Chrome Credential Harvester, SafeBoot & Rust/Go Multi-Platform Encryption
scenario.overview: Imagine a brick city apartment building entrance with a glass vestibule, a wall of brass resident mailboxes, a doorman podium, and a glowing brass intercom buzzer panel. Standing outside the locked glass apartment vestibule, an uninvited caller presses a crafted sequence on the brass intercom buzzer pretending to be building maintenance. In this real-world scenario, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the building doorman's station, then smuggles copied records out past the locked glass vestibule door in tiny disguised batches. The doorman checks the visitor sign-in ledger against the intercom buzz history and realizes no maintenance visit was ever scheduled by management. In this scenario (T1555.003, Sophos X-Ops, Trend Micro & Group-IB, Qilin , Agenda Ransomware: GPO PowerShell Chrome Credential Harvester, SafeBoot & Rust/Go Multi-Platform Encryption), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: active Directory GPO Logon Script Harvesting, then credential-Authenticated Share Mounting, then simultaneous Windows. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Active Directory GPO Logon Script Harvesting, then Credential-Authenticated Share Mounting, then Simultaneous Windows, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Active Directory GPO Logon Script Harvesting Chrome/Edge DPAPI Credentials
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1555.003 - Credentials from Web Browsers / T1484.001)
stages.description: Standing outside the locked glass apartment vestibule, an uninvited caller presses a crafted sequence on the brass intercom buzzer pretending to be building maintenance. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the building doorman's station while everyday visitors and the building doorman go about their routine. After compromising a Domain Controller, Qilin affiliates create a Group Policy Object linking a PowerShell logon script (\\corp.local\SYSVOL\corp.local\scripts\logon.ps1). Whenever any domain user logs in, the script copies %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data and Local State, decrypts the AES-GCM master key via ProtectedData::Unprotect under the user’s own session context, and writes the cleartext credentials to a staging share (logged in PowerShell Event 4104 with Technique=GPO-Driven Mass Browser Credential Harvesting , Sophos X-Ops, TargetArtifacts=Chrome/Edge Login Data SQLite + Local State DPAPI Key, MitreId=T1555.003 , Credentials from Web Browsers so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes GPO Logon Script: powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \\corp.local\SYSVOL\corp.local\scripts\logon.ps1 (which invokes the Windows PowerShell host , powershell.exe with stealth and execution-policy bypass flags , such as -NoP, -NonI, -W Hidden, -Exec Bypass so that achieves fileless in-memory staging and execution , T1555.003 during "Active Directory GPO Logon Script Harvesting Chrome/Edge DPAPI Credentials" without writing compiled binaries to disk, while generating PowerShell Operational EventID 4104 , ScriptBlock and 4103 , Module/Pipeline telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact [System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData]::Unprotect($encryptedKey, $null, 'CurrentUser') -> Dump Chrome Login Data SQLite to \\DC01\Temp$\creds.txt runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , [System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData]::Unprotect, $encryptedKey, $null, 'CurrentUser' so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1555.003 during "Active Directory GPO Logon Script Harvesting Chrome/Edge DPAPI Credentials" , After compromising a Domain Controller, Qilin affiliates create a Group Policy Object linking a PowerShell logon script , \\corp while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ powershell.exe / ⇠#1 ACK 4104) from Node ① (#1 Qilin / Agenda Affiliate Operator) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Windows Shares & ESXi Datastores (.qilin)).

stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement & Defense Evasion (T1021.002 / T1489 / T1490)
stages.description: Fooled by the caller’s voice over the lobby intercom, the building doorman buzzes open the interior lobby door and reads out the hallway elevator code. Here in Step 2 inside the apartment lobby, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the building doorman's station without disturbing the resident locked mailboxes. Using the harvested domain and vCenter/ESXi credentials, the operator invokes the Rust-compiled Qilin binary with -d DOMAIN\Admin:Password (which calls WNetAddConnection2W to automatically authenticate and mount inaccessible remote shares), stops 60+ backup and database services (veeam, sql, msexchange), and deletes Volume Shadow Copies (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with AutoMountSwitch=-d DOMAIN\User:Password , WNetAddConnection2W, TerminatedServices=VeeamBackupSvc, MSSQLSERVER, MSExchangeIS, Sophos so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
